name: Assembly Hall of Shame
tagline: Racing to the bottom of CPU performance
description: The Assembly Hall of Shame is a satirical but technically deep research effort that searches for the absolute floor of single-instruction CPU performance — the opposite of performance optimization. It documents a leaderboard of the slowest x86 instructions ever measured, from a humble nop at 1 cycle to the current champion, fxrstor64, which loads 512 bytes of FPU state from a high-latency MMIO region while a fleet of hammer cores starves the PCIe fabric — scoring 198,002,498,236 cycles and taking 62 seconds. The collection includes spec-violating unaligned loads used to break System Management Mode, strategies for saturating write-combining buffers, and MMIO deadspace hunting with companion tools. From the researcher behind MOVfuscator, it is a morbidly fascinating autopsy of absurd x86 code paths, with honest rules, reproducible measurements, and a roadmap for xrstor64 on AMX hardware.
highlights: Leaderboard of the slowest single instructions ever measured, from nop to fxrstor64
Champion scores 198 billion cycles by loading FPU state from MMIO while hammer cores starve the PCIe fabric
Spec-violating unaligned loads used to break System Management Mode
Companion tools: mmiotic for MMIO deadspace hunting and rakefield for high-latency CPUID leaves
Reproducible measurements with honest rules and normalized cycle counts
curatorNote: Fresh drop from xoreaxeaxeax, the researcher behind MOVfuscator — satirical but technically deep, racing to the bottom of CPU performance. It is the rare repo that makes you laugh and learn something about PCIe fabric in the same breath.
